title: When the Uniform Wakes
premise: In 1911, in the river town of Vellamark, Juniper Almeida hides her late father's revolutionary past behind an apprenticeship at the observatory, where she alone can service the master clock. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the guild ledger containing every name of the old resistance network—including forged entries that could condemn innocent families—Juniper realizes her invisibility was always someone else's design: the clockmaker who trained her hid the true ledger inside the clock itself. As the river ice thaws and checkpoints multiply, she must smuggle the evidence downstream to a sympathetic magistrate before the army burns the archives. She succeeds at devastating cost, losing her mentor and her anonymity, but gains a found family among the townsfolk who finally see her—and chooses to stay and rebuild rather than vanish again.
about_author: Dominic Okafor is a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring timepieces in coastal archive towns, where he collected the oral histories that seed his fiction. He writes about ordinary people caught in machinery larger than themselves, believing history turns on small hands doing quiet work.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She climbs the observatory tower to service the master clock, establishing her skill, her habit of invisibility, and her grief for her father. A small kindness to the night watchman, Bram, hints at her loneliness. Emotional beat: competent solitude masking fear of being known.

chapters.title: Requisition Orders
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Soldiers march into Vellamark; Captain Hessler posts notices claiming the town's records 'for security.' The guild panics. Her mentor, Master Corvin, goes pale at the mention of the ledger and orders her to say nothing. Emotional beat: dread arriving in polished boots.

chapters.title: What Corvin Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Searching Corvin's workshop for tools, she finds a hidden compartment with a key stamped with the observatory's serial number—and a photograph of her father with young Corvin. She confronts him; he admits the resistance ledger is real. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with revelation.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Corvin maps the town's new military geography: bridge, market gate, and dockhouse all search outgoing traffic. The ice on the river will break within weeks, ending barge travel. They agree the evidence must reach Magistrate Ilse Dorn before then. Emotional beat: a plan forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Clockmaker's Daughter
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The watchman watches Juniper move through the occupied streets and recognizes her father's walk, his same careful silence. He says nothing but begins leaving the tower door unlocked. Emotional beat: loyalty quietly choosing a side.

chapters.title: Hessler's Inspection
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Captain Hessler tours the observatory, fascinated by the clock, and questions Juniper about its maintenance history. She performs ignorance while terrified he'll ask about the case housing. He requisitions the tower as a signal station. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon pointed at her.

chapters.title: Names in the Margin
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Studying the seized public ledger's copy, she realizes the army has incomplete names—but the forger's hand matches Corvin's, meaning he protected people by falsifying records. Some of those people are her neighbors. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited secrets.

chapters.title: The Baker's Boy
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Fourteen-year-old Tomas, whose father's name is on the list, catches Juniper copying documents and blackmails his way into helping—not from courage, but terror. She reluctantly accepts. Emotional beat: found family beginning in mutual fear.

chapters.title: First Crossing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A test run: Tomas carries decoy papers through the market gate and is nearly caught when a soldier finds his bakery flour suspicious. Juniper improvises, vouching for him as her apprentice. Emotional beat: first bloodless escape, first bond sealed.

chapters.title: Corvin's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. He tells Juniper the full history: her father didn't die in the mill accident—he was executed, and Corvin forged the report. He hid the true ledger inside the clock's weight case, trusting only her hands could retrieve it unseen. Emotional beat: guilt handed down like an heirloom.

chapters.title: The Weight Case
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. During scheduled maintenance, before soldiers stationed in the tower, she extracts the oilskin-wrapped ledger from inside the driving weight, replacing it with ballast. The clock keeps perfect time. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by how easily she lied.

chapters.title: A Crack in the Ice
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The river groans; thaw is early this year. Hessler announces the docks close in ten days 'for the season'—actually to trap the network. Juniper realizes their window just shrank. Emotional beat: time becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: Bram's Debt
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A soldier recognizes Bram from an old regiment and offers him immunity for reporting 'unusual activity.' Bram, who owes Juniper's father his life, reports nothing—but knows he's now suspected either way. Emotional beat: loyalty priced in risk.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Someone tips Hessler that documents are moving. Searches intensify; a neighbor is detained. Juniper suspects the tailor's clerk who saw her at the gate. Paranoia fractures the town's fragile solidarity. Emotional beat: trust under interrogation.

chapters.title: Diversion at the Gate
chapters.summary: Juniper and Tomas's alternating POV. They stage a clock-tower malfunction—a striking mechanism gone wild—to pull guards from the bridge checkpoint while a courier crosses. It works, but Hessler notes the timing coincidence. Emotional beat: ingenuity spending its last credit.

chapters.title: Corvin Taken
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Soldiers arrest Corvin at dawn. Under questioning he gives them nothing, but they find his workshop compartment empty—the ledger missing—and know it exists. Hessler doubles every checkpoint and seals the tower. Emotional beat: the plan's architect paying its price.

chapters.title: What the Town Knew
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs—baker, ferryman, Bram. The town, which claimed ignorance for years, begins small acts of defiance: wrong directions given to patrols, a boat left unchained. Juniper sees she was never invisible; she was protected. Emotional beat: collective courage surfacing.

chapters.title: The Last Barge
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With the docks closing tomorrow, Juniper hides the ledger in the clock's pendulum bob and walks it past the tower guards as 'maintenance removal,' Tomas carrying her toolbox. At the dockhouse checkpoint, the ferryman lies about cargo. Emotional beat: the whole town complicit in one lie.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the water, a patrol boat hails the barge. Hessler himself boards, suspicious, and inspects the cargo inches from the hidden ledger. Bram arrives with a fabricated emergency at the observatory—the clock 'failing'—pulling Hessler back to shore. Emotional beat: salvation arriving through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She reaches Magistrate Dorn as the river ice shatters behind the barge. Dorn reads the ledger and issues warrants halting the burn order. But news comes: Corvin died in custody without confessing. Emotional beat: victory and grief in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Testimony of Springs and Gears
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the tribunal, Juniper testifies openly—her father's name, Corvin's forgeries made as mercy, the army's seizure unlawful. Hessler is relieved of command. She speaks not as an invisible apprentice but as a clockmaker, a daughter, a witness. Emotional beat: identity claimed at last.

chapters.title: Winding Forward
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Spring. Juniper takes over Corvin's workshop, takes Tomas as her apprentice, and shares Sunday dinners with Bram and the ferryman's family. She services the master clock still—but now the whole town knows whose hands keep it running. Emotional beat: a life wound tight with purpose, finally allowed to strike.
